short_description: Not a cell — the straw-yellow acellular liquid fraction of blood (~55 % of its volume, ~92 % water) in which every blood cell travels: dissolved albumin, Y-shaped antibodies, rod-like fibrinogen and a thousand other proteins, plus salts, glucose, hormones and dissolved gases; delivers nutrients everywhere and hauls waste to kidney and liver. Serum = plasma minus the clotting factors.

key_facts.albumin: ~35-50 g/L, ~50-60 % of plasma protein, 66.5 kDa, compact ~8 nm heart-shaped molecule, liver-made; oncotic pressure + cargo transport
key_facts.globulins: ~35-38 % of plasma protein, incl. Y-shaped IgG antibodies (~150 kDa, 10-15 nm) from plasma cells
key_facts.fibrinogen: 2-4 g/L, 340 kDa, elongated trinodular rod ~45-46 nm; soluble precursor of fibrin
key_facts.colour: straw-yellow / pale amber, mainly from bilirubin and carotenoids
key_facts.separated_column: plasma ~55 % on top, buffy coat <1 % (leukocytes+platelets), erythrocyte column ~45 % (haematocrit) at the bottom
key_facts.serum_caveat: serum = plasma minus fibrinogen and other clotting factors

rendering_honesty: A liquid cannot be micrographed. Per-style compositions: textbook = macroscopic separated/centrifuged column (the classic figure); 3d + watercolor + sem = molecular-scale zoom INTO the amber fluid (albumin blobs, Y-antibodies, trinodular fibrinogen rods; cells only as huge out-of-focus context). The sem slot is a false-colour molecular-surface visualization, NOT a real SEM modality — flagged in verdicts. The real reference is macroscopic photography, not microscopy.

reference.modality: macroscopic photograph (settled anticoagulated blood in a syringe; plasma layer on top) — not microscopy
